*   Shape MLP ($\text{MLP}_\theta$): Maps $\mathbf{x}$ to density $\sigma$ and normal $\mathbf{n}$.
*   Reflectance MLP ($\text{MLP}_\psi$): Maps $\mathbf{x}$ to BRDF parameters $(a, \gamma)$.

The method relies on three Multi-Layer Perceptrons (MLPs).
**Shape Network**: Input $\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^3$.
Outputs scalar density $\sigma \in \mathbb{R}$ and vector normal $\mathbf{n} \in \mathbb{R}^3$.
**Reflectance Network**: Input $\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^3$.
Outputs scalar albedo $a \in \mathbb{R}$ and scalar roughness parameter $\gamma \in \mathbb{R}$.
**Visibility Network**: Input $(\mathbf{x}, \boldsymbol{\omega}_i) \in \mathbb{R}^3 \times \mathbb{R}^3$.
Outputs scalar expected depth $\tilde{t}_0 \in \mathbb{R}$.
Draw $N=256$ stratified samples along the camera ray $\mathbf{x}(t) = \mathbf{c} - t\boldsymbol{\omega}_o$.
For each point $\mathbf{x}(t)$ along the ray, estimate the direct illumination integral.
Estimate indirect illumination for points along the ray.
*   **Visibility MLP Accuracy**: The method relies on $\text{MLP}_\phi$ to predict termination depths for both visibility occlusion and indirect ray bounces.
*   **Normal Estimation**: Normals are derived as the gradient of the shape network $\nabla_\mathbf{x} \text{MLP}_\theta$.
*   **Integration Error**: The integration of direct and indirect illumination uses discrete sampling (grid and random).
Each pixel requires 256 forward passes through the shape and reflectance networks.

Additionally, for every sample, direct illumination requires 288 queries to the visibility network and environment lighting lookup, and indirect illumination requires 128 queries to the visibility network plus shading of secondary points.
This makes it significantly slower than standard NeRF which typically does not perform explicit ray tracing for lighting.
*   **Memory Complexity**: Depends on the size of the three MLPs ($\theta, \psi, \phi$).
It extends neural volume rendering by decoupling geometry, reflectance, and visibility into separate neural fields to facilitate relighting.
